title: Well-defined poset structure on the induced space G ×^P X'
body_html:
Well-defined poset structure on the induced space

Fix the induction data $(G', P)$ satisfying (P0)–(P2) and the induced space $X = G \times^P X'$ of [[node:equivariant_sheaves.induction_GxP_X]], with $\iota : X' \hookrightarrow X$, $E \mapsto [(1, E)]$.

The face relation on $X$ is not automatic from the definition of $X$ as a set-theoretic quotient — it must be constructed and shown to descend to the quotient by $\sim$.

Definition (generator + reflexive-transitive closure)

Definition. The face relation $\preceq$ on $X = G \times^P X'$ is the smallest reflexive transitive relation on $X$ satisfying the following generator: $$ > \text{for every } g \in G \text{ and } F, E \in [\![X']\!] > \text{ with } F \preceq E \text{ in } X', \qquad > g \cdot \iota F \;\preceq\; g \cdot \iota E. > $$

Equivalently, $\preceq$ is the reflexive-transitive closure of the generator relation ${(g \cdot \iota F, g \cdot \iota E) : g \in G,\, F \preceq E \text{ in } X'}$ on the quotient $X$. The chain condition on $X'$ (strict monotonicity of $\dim$ along proper faces) carries over: reflexivity is the $F = E$ case; transitivity is the closure axiom.

Equivalent characterisation

The reflexive-transitive closure form is elegant but not immediately usable for calculation. The following point-wise characterisation gives a single-quantifier form used throughout the induction / QFD proofs:

Theorem (single-witness characterisation). For representatives $(g_1, E_1), (g_2, E_2) \in G \times X'$, $$ > [(g_1, E_1)] \;\preceq\; [(g_2, E_2)] > \;\iff\; > \exists\, n \in G',\quad n \cdot E_1 \preceq E_2 \text{ in } X' > \;\;\text{and}\;\; g_1^{-1} g_2 n \in P_{E_1}. > $$

Note the parallel with the equivalence relation $\sim$ of [[node:equivariant_sheaves.induction_GxP_X]]: replacing $\preceq$ on $X'$ by $=$ recovers $\sim$ verbatim.

Proof (theorem). ($\Leftarrow$) Given $n \in G'$ with the stated properties, we exhibit a two-step chain $[(g_1, E_1)] \;\sim\; [(g_2, n \cdot E_1)] \;\preceq_{\text{gen}}\; [(g_2, E_2)]$:

  • Equivalence step. Apply the definition of $\sim$ with witness $m := n \in G'$: $m \cdot E_1 = n \cdot E_1$ (trivially), and $g_1^{-1} g_2 m = g_1^{-1} g_2 n \in P_{E_1}$ by hypothesis. So $(g_1, E_1) \sim (g_2, n \cdot E_1)$.
  • Generator step. From $n \cdot E_1 \preceq E_2$ in $X'$ and the generator with $F = n \cdot E_1$, $E = E_2$, $g = g_2$: $g_2 \cdot \iota(n \cdot E_1) \preceq g_2 \cdot \iota E_2$, i.e. $[(g_2, n \cdot E_1)] \preceq [(g_2, E_2)]$.

Combining: $[(g_1, E_1)] \preceq [(g_2, E_2)]$.

($\Rightarrow$) The single-witness form is reflexive (take $n = 1$), contains all generators (take $n = 1$), and is transitive under (P0)+(P1) (see below). Hence it contains the reflexive-transitive closure. $\square$

The single-witness form is precisely the pre-quotient face relation $\preceq_{\text{rep}}$ on $G \times X'$: $$ (g_1, E_1) \preceq_{\text{rep}} (g_2, E_2) \;:\iff\; \exists\, n \in G',\;\; n \cdot E_1 \preceq E_2 \;\text{and}\; g_1^{-1} g_2 n \in P_{E_1}. $$

Proposition: $\preceq_{\text{rep}}$ descends to a partial order

Proposition. Under (P0)–(P2), $\preceq_{\text{rep}}$ on $G \times X'$ satisfies:

  1. Reflexivity. $(g, E) \preceq_{\text{rep}} (g, E)$.
  2. Transitivity. $(g_1, E_1) \preceq_{\text{rep}} (g_2, E_2)$ and $(g_2, E_2) \preceq_{\text{rep}} (g_3, E_3)$ imply $(g_1, E_1) \preceq_{\text{rep}} (g_3, E_3)$.
  3. Left descent. If $(g_1, E_1) \sim (g_1', E_1')$ then $(g_1, E_1) \preceq_{\text{rep}} (h, F) \iff (g_1', E_1') \preceq_{\text{rep}} (h, F)$.
  4. Right descent. If $(h, F) \sim (h', F')$ then $(g, E) \preceq_{\text{rep}} (h, F) \iff (g, E) \preceq_{\text{rep}} (h', F')$.
  5. Antisymmetry modulo $\sim$. If both $(g_1, E_1) \preceq_{\text{rep}} (g_2, E_2)$ and $(g_2, E_2) \preceq_{\text{rep}} (g_1, E_1)$, then $(g_1, E_1) \sim (g_2, E_2)$.

Consequently, $\preceq$ on $X = (G \times X')/{\sim}$ is a well-defined partial order and coincides with both the reflexive-transitive closure of the generators (by the theorem) and the descent of $\preceq_{\text{rep}}$.
proof_html:
of the proposition

(1) Reflexivity. Take $n := 1 \in G'$. Then $1 \cdot E = E \preceq E$ and $g^{-1} g \cdot 1 = 1 \in P_E$.

(2) Transitivity. Given witnesses $n_1$ for $(g_1, E_1) \preceq_{\text{rep}} (g_2, E_2)$ and $n_2$ for $(g_2, E_2) \preceq_{\text{rep}} (g_3, E_3)$, take $n := n_2 n_1 \in G'$.

Face-chain: $(n_2 n_1) \cdot E_1 = n_2 \cdot (n_1 \cdot E_1) \preceq n_2 \cdot E_2 \preceq E_3$ using cellularity ($n_2$ preserves $\preceq$) and transitivity of $\preceq$ on $X'$.

Membership: from $g_1^{-1} g_2 n_1 \in P_{E_1}$ and $g_2^{-1} g_3 n_2 \in P_{E_2}$:

  • By (P0) and $n_1 \cdot E_1 \preceq E_2$: $P_{E_2} \le P_{n_1 \cdot E_1}$, so $g_2^{-1} g_3 n_2 \in P_{n_1 \cdot E_1}$.
  • By (P1): $P_{n_1 \cdot E_1} = n_1 P_{E_1} n_1^{-1}$, so there exists $p \in P_{E_1}$ with $n_1 p n_1^{-1} = g_2^{-1} g_3 n_2$.
  • Rearranging: $g_1^{-1} g_3 (n_2 n_1) = (g_1^{-1} g_2 n_1) \cdot p \in P_{E_1} \cdot P_{E_1} = P_{E_1}$.

(3) Left descent. Suppose $(g_1, E_1) \sim (g_1', E_1')$ with witness $m \in G'$: $m \cdot E_1 = E_1'$ and $g_1^{-1} g_1' m \in P_{E_1}$. Assume $(g_1, E_1) \preceq_{\text{rep}} (h, F)$ with witness $n$. Take $n'' := n m^{-1} \in G'$:

  • Face-chain: $n'' \cdot E_1' = n m^{-1} \cdot (m \cdot E_1) = n \cdot E_1 \preceq F$.
  • Membership: write $g_1^{-1} g_1' m = \alpha \in P_{E_1}$. Then $(g_1')^{-1} h n'' = m \alpha^{-1} g_1^{-1} h n m^{-1}$; substitute $g_1^{-1} h n \in P_{E_1}$ and use (P1) with $m$ to conclude $m \alpha^{-1} (g_1^{-1} h n) m^{-1} \in m P_{E_1} m^{-1} = P_{m \cdot E_1} = P_{E_1'}$.

The reverse implication is symmetric via $m^{-1}$.

(4) Right descent. Suppose $(h, F) \sim (h', F')$ with witness $m$. Assume $(g, E) \preceq_{\text{rep}} (h, F)$ with witness $n$. Take $n'' := m n \in G'$:

  • Face-chain: $n'' \cdot E = m \cdot (n \cdot E) \preceq m \cdot F = F'$.
  • Membership: write $h^{-1} h' m = \alpha \in P_F$. By (P0) with $n \cdot E \preceq F$: $\alpha \in P_F \le P_{n \cdot E}$. By (P1): $\alpha = n p n^{-1}$ for some $p \in P_E$. Compute $g^{-1} h' n'' = (g^{-1} h n) \cdot p$; both factors lie in $P_E$.

(5) Antisymmetry modulo $\sim$. From $(g_1, E_1) \preceq_{\text{rep}} (g_2, E_2)$ via $n_1$ and the reverse via $n_2$, we obtain $(n_2 n_1) \cdot E_1 \preceq E_1$. Because the $G$-action is cellular it preserves dimension (Cellular G-action on an abstract cell complex): $\dim((n_2 n_1) \cdot E_1) = \dim E_1$. Strict monotonicity of $\dim$ along a proper face-chain (Abstract cell complex) then forces $(n_2 n_1) \cdot E_1 = E_1$, hence $n_1 \cdot E_1 = E_2$ (and the $P_{E_1}$-membership from the $n_1$-witness is exactly the $\sim$-witness). $\square$

Which axioms feed into which clause

Clause Axioms used
Definition (generator + refl-trans closure) none (structural)
Theorem (single-witness ⇔ closure) (P0), (P1), plus (P2) is not needed
Reflexivity none (unit in $G'$, unit in $P_E$)
Transitivity (P0), (P1)
Left descent (P1)
Right descent (P0), (P1)
Antisymmetry mod ∼ dim preservation (cellular action) + strict monotonicity

Note: (P2) enters the equivalence relation via ι : X' → G ×^P X' is a cellular embedding (poset form) clause (1) (injectivity of $\iota$), not the face relation.

Consequences

  • The embedding $\iota : X' \to G \times^P X'$, $E \mapsto [(1, E)]$, is order-preserving and order-reflecting; this is ι : X' → G ×^P X' is a cellular embedding (poset form) clause (2).
  • The dimension function $\dim([(g, E)]) := \dim E$ is well-defined because $\sim$ implies dimension-equal (from $n \cdot E_1 = E_2$ and dimension-preservation of the $G$-action).
  • Together with local finiteness of $X'$ (inherited via $G$-translates), this equips $G \times^P X'$ with the abstract-cell-complex and $G$-cell-complex instances that CW structure and QFD property on G ×^P X' uses as its poset-level content.

Lean formalization

The pre-quotient relation is exposed as the single-witness form (the name mirrors InductionRel for the equivalence relation):

def InductionLe (g₁E₁ g₂E₂ : G × X') : Prop :=
  ∃ n ∈ d.G', n • g₁E₁.2 ≤ g₂E₂.2 ∧
              g₁E₁.1⁻¹ * g₂E₂.1 * n ∈ d.P g₁E₁.2

Using the single-witness form as the primary Lean definition (rather than a Relation.ReflTransGen over generators) keeps the proofs elementary — each of the five clauses of the proposition then has a dedicated lemma:

Clause Lean lemma
(1) Reflexivity InductionLe_refl
(2) Transitivity InductionLe_trans
(3) Left descent InductionLe_left_descends
(4) Right descent InductionLe_right_descends
(5) Antisymmetry InductionLe_antisymm

The PartialOrder instance on InducedSpace d is built by Quotient.lift₂ (InductionLe d) — clauses (3) + (4) discharge the well-definedness side condition of Quotient.lift₂; clauses (1) + (2) discharge reflexivity and transitivity of the descended le; clause (5) discharges antisymmetry.

instance : PartialOrder (InducedSpace d) where
  le := Quotient.lift₂ (InductionLe d) ⟨left/right descent⟩
  le_refl  := ⟨InductionLe_refl⟩
  le_trans := ⟨InductionLe_trans⟩
  le_antisymm := ⟨InductionLe_antisymm⟩

The theorem "single-witness form ⇔ reflexive-transitive closure of the generator" is not separately formalised in the current library: the closure form serves as the mathematical definition, the single-witness form as the operational one, and they are known to coincide by the elementary two-step chain given above. An explicit Relation.ReflTransGen-based alternative definition plus an equivalence lemma is a well-scoped follow-up.
